\paragraph{Refined negative-weight subtraction.} Refinement used the unfold's deterministic GBDT configuration, independent injection and subtraction halves of background simulation, and bootstrap replicas that individually resampled every pseudo-event and refit refinement. It preserves the signed total to $3\times10^{-6}$ and clips \SIrange{0.01}{0.05}{\percent} of events. Corner bias falls from \SI{1.66}{\percent} to \SI{0.24}{\percent}, but residuals in some joint cells fail the nominal closure criterion. The criterion has two parts, each applied to all 153 reported quantities. No quantity may have a mean residual beyond 3.6 standard errors of the mean ($|t|>3.6$), a fixed threshold at about the two-sided 5\% level for a normal reference, Bonferroni-corrected over the 153. Nor may any quantity have a mean residual beyond half its bootstrap standard deviation with $|t|>3$. The data difference's sign pattern matches simulated purity bias at an order of magnitude smaller size; the difference is method sensitivity, not a measured bias. With either treatment, the estimator does not follow generator-sized $\Eavail$ shape changes. This refinement study ran no coverage test. Reducing one bias does not itself qualify an uncertainty, so this result does not close the revisit of the background treatment of the configuration-(a) five-dimensional central value (\S\ref{sec:negweight-footing}).

\paragraph{Refinement capacity.} Stay-Positive classifier underfitting causes the residual nominal bias of the refined subtraction. At the unfold's GBDT setting (100 trees, 8 leaves), the positive-weight probability is underfit, leaving up to \SI{4}{\percent} reco-level subtraction error per $(\Eavail,W)$ reco cell. With 400 trees and 31 leaves, error falls to \SI{1.7}{\percent}, paired truth-level bias falls by more than \SI{80}{\percent} in every affected cell, and nominal background-inclusive closure passes on 20 development and 40 fresh pseudo-experiments. Splitting background simulation into independent injection and subtraction halves is not the cause.

column8: \subsubsection{Closure tests across dimensions}
\label{sec:closure-map}

Only the MINERvA simulation supplies a detector response, the conditional distribution of reconstructed events given truth. Other generators (GiBUU, NuWro, GENIE variants) supply truth only. Every closure test here therefore keeps the simulated MINERvA response and changes the truth distribution, by reweighting the simulated events, or changes the analysis chain around it. Reweighting to another generator's shape is a valid known-truth test of the unfolding. It does not test the detector model. An ordinary closure, whose pseudo-data are the simulation itself, is an identity check that a constant estimator would also pass. \paragraph{Comparison of injected-bump and generator-shaped closure tests.} The injected-bump and generator-shaped tests differ in deformation, metric and iteration dependence. Their results do not contradict each other.
\begin{itemize}

\item \emph{Deformation.} The closing injections are single smooth bumps in one variable the classifiers see directly. A generator ratio changes correlated structure across $\Eavail$, $W$ and $q_3$, including directions the reconstructed observables constrain weakly (\S\ref{sec:val-departure}, comparison with exact binned unfolding).

\item \emph{Metric.} The 3D, 4D and 5D closures are judged on one-dimensional marginals, where per-cell errors average out. The 3D test's per-bin spread is already \SI{3.2}{\percent}, and the 5D test's is \SI{3.7}{\percent}. The generator-shaped failures are measured in joint $(\Eavail,W)$ cells.

\item \emph{Iterations.} At five iterations the estimator retains part of the prior wherever the reconstructed data constrain the truth weakly. Thirty iterations reduce the $\Eavail$ residual by \SI{26}{\percent} while the $q_3$ residual grows (\S\ref{sec:val-departure}).

\item \emph{Five-dimensional $W$ test.} A $W$ bump at the $\Delta$ peak is recovered to a ratio of 0.180 against a threshold of 0.20, a narrow pass in the marginal only. The same unfolding result leaves joint $(\Eavail,W)$ cells in the peak column up to \SI{9.4}{\percent} low and moves part of the bump into the neighboring $W$ bins. A single smooth bump in a marginal is therefore weaker evidence than the generator-shaped tests, which remain the main five-dimensional recovery evidence of \S\ref{sec:5d}.
\end{itemize}

Reweighted pseudo-data are unfolded with the unchanged CV response and compared with the reweighted truth marginal. Two shapes are tested: \texttt{gauss\_pt}, $f = 1 + A\exp\!\big[-((\pT - p_{T}^{0})/\sigma)^{2}\big]$ with $A=0.2$, $p_{T}^{0}=0.4$ GeV/c, $\sigma=0.1$ GeV/c; and \texttt{tilt\_pz}, $f = 1 + \alpha(\pPar - \pPar^{\text{ref}})$ with $\alpha=0.1$, $\pPar^{\text{ref}}=5$ GeV/c.
\subsubsection{Hidden-variable closure}
\label{sec:closure-hv}

OmniFold sees reco and truth $(\pT,\pPar)$ but excludes resolution variable $\dpT \equiv \pT^{\text{reco}}-\pT^{\text{truth}}$. A bias confined to this hidden axis tests leakage into the measured marginal. Pseudo-data receive
\begin{equation}
w^{\text{reco}}
w^{\text{reco}}\cdot
\Big(1 + A\exp\!\big[-((\dpT - c)/\sigma_{\dpT})^{2}\big]\Big),
\end{equation}

with $c=+0.1$ GeV/c, $\sigma_{\dpT}=0.05$ GeV/c, and amplitude scanned over $A\in\{0.05,0.10,0.30\}$. Truth weights are \emph{unchanged}, so the reference is the unaltered CV truth marginal. For median per-bin signed residual $\bar r(A)$, a linear fit gives $\bar r(A) \approx \kappa_{\text{leak}} A$, with $\kappa_{\text{leak}} = \partial \bar r/\partial A$, the fraction of hidden $\dpT$ bias entering the visible answer. The $3.0\%$ acceptance bound is looser than the truth-reweight bound because the weak $\dpT$--$\pT$ correlation prevents complete removal of the leakage.
\subsubsection{Alternative-model closure}
\label{sec:closure-alt}

The OmniFold response is trained on the CV weights and the pseudo-data are built from an alternative-universe reweighting: \texttt{MaCCQE:0} ($+1\sigma$), which probes an interaction-model shape change, or \texttt{Flux:50} (PPFX index $50$), which probes flux reweighting --- two distinct kinds of model dependence. The reference is the in-acceptance-extrapolated alternative truth,
\begin{equation}
\tilde X^{\text{ref}}_{i}
X^{\CV,\text{truth}}_{i}\cdot
\frac{X^{\text{alt},\text{in-acc}}_{i}}{X^{\CV,\text{in-acc}}_{i}},
\end{equation}

column8: \paragraph{Hidden-variable and alternative-model closures.} On the $205$ reported bins the per-amplitude median residuals, $0.57\% / 1.14\% / 3.43\%$ for $A = 0.05/0.10/0.30$, are linear in $A$, as expected for small perturbations, with fitted slope $\kappa_{\text{leak}} = \boxed{0.113}$ (App.~\ref{sec:closure-hv}): about $11\%$ of a hidden $\dpT$ bias leaks into the measured $(\pT,\pPar)$ marginal. Against the $3.0\%$ acceptance bound, two of the three arms pass and the largest does not: $A=0.30$ gives $3.43\%$, which \emph{exceeds} $3.0\%$ (Table~\ref{tab:closure-map}).
